---
title: "Module 14 — What Should Stay Python?"
---

## Goal

Resist the urge to move everything into Rust. Know when Python is the right home.

## Examples that often stay in Python

```python
agent.ask(...)
llm.generate(...)
mqtt.publish(...)
home_assistant.call_service(...)
workflow.execute(...)
```

## Typical reasons to remain in Python

| Reason                         | Why it matters |
|--------------------------------|----------------|
| Network latency dominates      | Native speed is irrelevant |
| Rapid experimentation          | Python iteration speed wins |
| Ecosystem integration          | Rich libraries already exist |
| Implementation changes often   | Avoid rewriting native code |
| Performance is irrelevant      | Clarity beats micro-optimisation |
| Orchestration readability      | Agents and workflows are easier to follow |

## The course principle restated

> Do not introduce Rust merely to eliminate Python.

Rust earns its place when the implementation is part of the **platform contract**: shared semantics, validation, deterministic evaluation, portable domain logic.

Python remains the flexible orchestration and AI environment.

## Decision checklist

Ask for each component:

1. Is there a single definition of “correct” that many consumers must share?
2. Would an incorrect implementation silently break the platform?
3. Do we need the same logic from Python, CLI, and possibly WASM?
4. Have we measured a real performance problem?

If most answers are “no”, keep it in Python.
